prompt: The five-number summary of a data set is Min = 9, Q1 = 12, Median = 15, Q3 = 18, Max = 21. Determine the interquartile range (IQR), and explain what it measures that the range does not.
answer: IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 18 − 12 = 6. The range is 21 − 9 = 12, which is decided entirely by the two most extreme values. The IQR measures the spread of the middle half of the data, so a single unusually large or small value cannot change it.
explanation: IQR = Q3 − Q1, and it is the more trustworthy of the two measures of spread. The range uses only the largest and smallest values, so one unusual reading moves it a long way; the IQR ignores the bottom quarter and the top quarter altogether and describes where the middle half of the data sits. That is why a box-and-whisker plot draws the box from Q1 to Q3: the box IS the IQR.

prompt: Determine the mode of the data set.
explanation: The mode is the value that appears most often. 53 appears 2 times and every other value appears once, so the mode is 53. A data set can have more than one mode, or none at all if every value appears the same number of times — but it is never an average of anything, which is the usual confusion with the mean.
